messages:
maya: quick design pitch — thinking about introducing 'token silos' so API keys can be pinned to project-level routing pools. goal: prevent noisy tenants from spilling Dedicated capacity across orgs and make quota attribution simpler. doc: https://go/redwood/token-silos (WIP)
aj: quick q — how do silos interact with quotas? if token is pinned to proj, does quota live on proj or org?
maya: plan is proj-scoped quota for pinned tokens. org-scoped tokens keep org quota. migration path for legacy org tokens -> option to opt-in per-org.
samir: console impact: we should add a visual to show which tokens are siloed and their target pool. feature flag like `token_silo_visualizer` so ops can toggle. also need telemetry: route_hits, route_misses, fallback_count for siloed tokens.
toni: my main worry: fallback behavior. if proj pool is full, we must not route to another org's Dedicated pool. fallback must go to hosted or shared tier. otherwise we defeat isolation.
maya: agreed. fallback policy: project-pinned -> hosted fallback only. cluster routing config (pseudo):
```yaml
routing: 
  - match: token.scope == \"project:123\"
    prefer: dedicated-pool:proj-123
  - fallback: hosted
```
aj: telemetry suggestion: emit `token_silo_route_miss{project=\"123\"}` and a histogram for latency when fallback occurs. that will catch perf cliffs.
samir: console UX: show fallback history per-token -> small timeline with counts, last 30d. add quick revoke button for admins. also require an approval step for auto-migrating legacy tokens into silos.
toni: rollout plan idea: canary 1% orgs, then 10% with strict monitoring on `quota_denied` and `fallback_rate`. tie to automatic rollbacks if fallback_rate > 1% in 15m window.
maya: migration script draft: `legacy_token_migration.py` will idempotently create project bindings using a best-effort mapping (owner email -> project). will log ambiguous cases to a ticket queue instead of auto-binding.
aj: what about service accounts used by infra? they often span projects. do we allow multi-project service tokens?
samir: we can introduce `service-account` tokens that carry allowlist of projects (small list) and treat them as multi-silo tokens; additional audit trail required. Keep default conservative.
maya: security note: telemetry must not include token material. emit token_id hashes only and scrub user-facing logs. update event schema: `token_event{token_hash=..., outcome=..., route=...}`.
deploy-bot: deploy: routing-config-prototype -> canary started for eng-team at 2024-11-01 15:22 UTC :rocket:
aj: ok, next steps: write up canary playbook, add metrics to prometheus, wire console flag. i'll take metrics.
samir: i'll prototype console card and feature flag toggle.
toni: i'll write the fallback enforcement tests and mock Dedicated exhaustion scenarios.
maya: thanks — will push the WIP doc updates and link PRs. :+1:
